headline: Lead AI Product Designer
positioning: I design AI products and the design systems behind them, so that what a model produces is something a person can check, trust and act on.
summary: I'm Mohammad Abdul Aleem, a Lead AI Product Designer in Hyderabad. Thirteen-plus years in enterprise UX taught me that trust is a design outcome: it comes from clear states, honest copy, accessible components and systems that behave the same way every time.
Today I spend most of my time on design systems that engineers and AI agents can both consume, and on the product flows where a model's output meets a person who has to act on it.

principles.title: Trust is designed, not declared
principles.body: Every AI state, thinking, unsure, wrong, recovering, gets a deliberate design. A confident UI over an uncertain model is a lie users eventually catch.

principles.title: Ship the system, not the screen
principles.body: Tokens, components and spec files outlive any single mock-up. If an engineer or an agent can't rebuild it from the spec, it isn't done.

principles.title: Accessible by default
principles.body: WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor, checked in code, not a final-week audit. It is also the fastest way to make AI output readable by everyone.

aiWorkflow.title: Understand the workflow
aiWorkflow.body: I start with the business problem and how the work is done today, before any screen.

aiWorkflow.title: Redesign it
aiWorkflow.body: I redraw the workflow around the person who has to act, and decide where a model helps and where a person must check.

aiWorkflow.title: Build it with AI
aiWorkflow.body: I use Claude and other generative tools every day for UI exploration, interaction design, documentation and reusable prompts, working from a design system so the output stays on-system.

aiWorkflow.title: Validate it with people
aiWorkflow.body: I prototype, test with users and stay with the work through design-to-development handoff until it is in production.
